section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Symphony of Waves
section_1.content: Introduce the core concept: any complex periodic signal can be broken down into a sum of simple sine and cosine waves. Use a visual of a 'digital musical synthesizer' combining basic tones to create a complex voice.
section_1.example: Imagine a digital 'singing cat'—the complex meow is actually a collection of simple, overlapping pure-tone sine waves.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: Orthogonality of Sinusoids
section_2.content: Briefly explain the 'Basis' concept. Just as 2D space uses X and Y axes, signal space uses sine and cosine functions. Emphasize that these functions are 'orthogonal' (they don't overlap in a way that interferes), allowing us to isolate each individual frequency component.
section_2.example: Visualize two perpendicular vectors; moving in the X-direction tells you nothing about the Y-direction—this 'independence' is the key to extracting coefficients.

section_3.title: The Mathematical Recipe: Defining the Series
section_3.content: Present the Fourier Series formula: f(t) = a0/2 + Σ[an cos(nωt) + bn sin(nωt)]. Explain that a0, an, and bn are the 'weights' or 'volume knobs' for each frequency component.
section_3.example: Animation showing an equalizer: each coefficient is a slider adjusting the height of a specific sine wave frequency.

section_4.title: Visualizing the Synthesis
section_4.content: Demonstrate the additive process. Start with a single sine wave, then add the 2nd harmonic, 3rd, and so on. Show how the summation gradually begins to resemble a 'Square Wave' (the classic pedagogical example).
section_4.example: An animation of a robotic arm tracing a circular path; as more 'epicycles' (harmonics) are added, the circular path sharpens into the corners of a square.

section_5.title: Application & Conclusion
section_5.content: Discuss real-world utility: Compression (MP3/JPEG) and Signal Filtering. Summarize that Fourier Series turns time-domain confusion into frequency-domain clarity.
section_5.example: A smartphone using Fourier analysis to identify a bird’s chirp in a noisy forest by isolating the unique frequency 'fingerprint' of the bird.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Orthogonality of Sinusoids", [
            "Sine and cosine functions form a signal basis.",
            "Orthogonality ensures these components are independent.",
            "This independence allows us to isolate frequencies."
        ])
        
        # Setup visual elements
        wave1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=BLUE)
        wave2 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * np.pi * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=RED)
        label1 = MathTex(r"f_1(t)", color=BLUE)
        label2 = MathTex(r"f_2(t)", color=RED)
        integral_eq = MathTex(r"\int_0^T f_1(t)f_2(t)dt = 0", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(wave1, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, 'B1', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(wave1), Write(label1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.place_at_grid(wave2, 'C2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label2, 'C1', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(wave2), Write(label2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(integral_eq, 'E2', 'F5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(integral_eq))
        self.wait(2)
